samples.text:
The table give information about the average hours that full-time workers work each week and how many days of paid holiday and public holidays they have in six countries in 2023.

Looking at working hours, Country D has the longest week with 44.6 hours, then Country F with 42.3 hours and Country B with 41.8 hours. Country C workers work 39.2 hours. On the other hand, Country A has the shortest working week, only 36.5 hours, and Country E is similar with 37.9 hours.

About paid holiday, Country A is the highest with 30 days and Country E has 28 days. Country C also have a lot, 25 days. However, Country B workers only get 10 days, which is the lowest, and Country D get 14 days. Country F is in the middle with 20 days.

For public holidays, the numbers is more similar. Country D has the most with 16 days, and Country E has the least with 8 days. The others are between 9 and 13 days.

Overall, the countries where people works longer hours usually have less paid holiday.
samples.why: All three columns covered accurately but described separately with little comparison · brief overview at the end · repetitive linking and verbs · several subject–verb agreement errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The table compares six countries in terms of the average number of hours full-time employees worked per week in 2023, together with their entitlement to paid annual leave and the number of public holidays.

Overall, there appears to be an inverse relationship between working hours and paid holiday: countries with shorter working weeks generally offer considerably more annual leave. Public holidays, by contrast, vary much less between the countries.

Country A has the shortest average week, at 36.5 hours, and also the most generous holiday allowance, with 30 days. Country E and Country C follow a similar pattern, with working weeks of 37.9 and 39.2 hours respectively and 28 and 25 days of paid leave.

At the other end of the scale, employees in Country D work the longest hours, averaging 44.6 per week, yet they receive only 14 days of paid holiday. Similarly, workers in Country F and Country B put in 42.3 and 41.8 hours, and are entitled to 20 and 10 days respectively, with Country B's figure being the lowest in the table. As for public holidays, these range from 8 days in Country E to 16 in Country D, which partly compensate for its limited annual leave.
samples.why: Clear overview identifying the link between hours and leave · countries logically grouped · range of cohesive devices, slightly heavy use of respectively · good collocations · one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The table sets out the average weekly working hours of full-time employees in six countries in 2023, alongside the number of days of paid annual leave and public holidays they received.

Longer working weeks generally go hand in hand with less paid leave, whereas the number of public holidays varies within a narrow range and does not follow the same pattern.

Country A offers the most favourable conditions, combining the shortest average week of 36.5 hours with the largest leave entitlement of 30 days. Countries E and C are broadly comparable, with employees working 37.9 and 39.2 hours respectively and receiving 28 and 25 days of paid holiday. When public holidays are included, workers in these three countries enjoy between 36 and 39 days off a year.

The picture is markedly different in Countries D, F and B, where average hours exceed 41. Country D has the longest working week, at 44.6 hours, and just 14 days of annual leave, although its 16 public holidays are the highest figure in the table. Country B stands out for the least generous leave allowance of only 10 days, a third of that in Country A, despite a working week of 41.8 hours, while Country F sits between these extremes at 42.3 hours and 20 days.
samples.why: Insightful overview contrasting leave with public holidays · data grouped and synthesised (combined days off) · seamless cohesion · precise, flexible vocabulary · wide range of structures, error-free.
